items.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: And this friend of mine, a tenor player, brought Jackie in to hear our quartet.

ctx.x: No. I met him when I was 17 I believe it was. And he had another girlfriend, and I was just this little naive girl from Milwaukee you know. So I don’t think I attracted his attention that much. But then he did like working with me I believe.

Here’s what happened. A friend of mine brought her in to the club, Jump Town, it was early ‘47, on the west end of Chicago. Dave Garroway was looking for sponsors. Jump Town was his first sponsor. He talked up the club. He talked it up, talked it up, the place starts to boom. And this friend of mine, a tenor player, brought Jackie in to hear our quartet. I was working with the George Davis Quartet. It was alto, piano, bass and drums. And this tenor player said, “hey let her sing, she’s really good.” And I says,…

Piano players never like to play for girl singers, because half the time they don’t know what key they sing and they don’t know what tune they want to do, and that sort of thing. So they’re sort of negative about it in general.
